issues.title: [EPIC] M1-harness — Harness & inference layer
issues.body:
> Milestone of the [Petri v2 migration tracker](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) (#100).

## Goal

Ship the v2 inference layer: first-party pydantic-ai Model subclasses for pi (--mode rpc, default for fresh dishes) and the Claude Code CLI, plus passthrough for any provider string from petri.yaml. The v1 engine keeps working; an opt-in bridge runs petri seed and petri grow on the dish's selected backend. Zero-API-key subscription auth survives the move (D3/D5).

## Shipping

petri-grow 0.4.0: a harness: block in petri.yaml picks pi, Claude Code, or a provider string, petri inspect preflights pi and Node, and dishes without the block behave exactly as v0.3.4. Ships with docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md and docs/field-reports.md, the reference docs every v2 issue cites.

## Steps

- [x] 1. #17 — Spike pi --mode rpc and the Node dependency story *(done — deliverables and transcripts on closed PR #119, kept as the record)*
- [ ] 2. #16 — Finalize ARCHITECTURE-V2: ADRs and module-fate audit *(docs only; parallel)*
- [ ] 3. #19 — Add TestModel and FunctionModel offline fixtures *(parallel)*
- [ ] 4. #24 — Extract prompt builders into reasoning/prompts.py *(parallel; good first issue)*
- [ ] 5. #120 — **Wire up the pi harness end-to-end** *(tracking issue for the pi chain: #18 → #20 → #21 → #22 → #25 → #26 → #27; cross-deps outside the chain: #22 and #26 also need #19, #26 also needs #24, #25 also needs #23; #27 closes the milestone)*
- [ ] 6. #23 — Port the Claude Code CLI to a ClaudeCodeModel *(after #18 and #19; parallel with the pi chain)*

## Risks

- ~~pi protocol assumptions may not survive the spike~~ — resolved: the spike validated the protocol (evidence on closed PR #119); fallbacks --mode json and -p confirmed working, and PiRpcTransport keeps pi swappable.
- pydantic-ai Model ABC signatures came from docs; every Model issue verifies against installed 2.9.0 and pins >=2.9,<3.
- Defaulting fresh dishes to pi can strand users without Node; preflight, the claude-code backend, and unchanged existing dishes cover it. The spike confirmed a Node-free standalone pi binary as the documented install path (Node ≥22.19 applies to the npm path only).
- Bridged runs lose WebSearch/WebFetch on backends without equivalents (the fabricated-citation risk from commit 7eee82b); M1 documents the gap, M2-agents closes it. Confirmed by the spike: pi ships no web tools; its extension API can supply them.
- Backend retries must be configurable to zero before M4-dbos wraps calls in DBOS steps; petri/harness/retry.py designs for that now. The spike adds: disable pi's own auto-retry (set_auto_retry) so Petri owns all throttling.

issues.body:
> Milestone of the [Petri v2 migration tracker](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) (#100).

## Goal

Move the 13-agent roster (3 leads, 10 specialists) onto pydantic-ai. Structure (roster, phases, blocking, debates, convergence) becomes typed code per D9; petri.yaml keeps content (instructions, verdict vocabularies, pairings, per-agent model). socratic_questioner sits outside the roster enum; the v0.3.x pipeline stays untouched.

## Shipping

A petri agents group: list renders the roster, check validates a dish's petri.yaml naming the offending key, and run executes one specialist end-to-end with a typed verdict, source-policy enforcement, real token accounting, and hard UsageLimits caps. Convergence and debates ship as unit-tested library code (TestModel/FunctionModel) for M4-dbos to wire in.

issues.title: [EPIC] M3-decomposer — Agentic decomposer + evals
issues.body:
> Milestone of the [Petri v2 migration tracker](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) (#100).

## Goal

Rebuild claim decomposition as a pydantic-ai agent subsystem (D6): typed outputs with retry, bedrock stops, counterargument children, code-enforced per-parent caps, and a search_cells tool that links colonies instead of duplicating cells. Add seed safety (overwrite guard, --resume, edit-at-approval) and the storage spine: a per-dish petri.sqlite domain store with an events/cells/edges schema (amended D4). A pydantic_evals suite measures quality against the field numbers: 9.7x cell inflation, ~25% trivial axioms, zero cross-colony references.

## Shipping

A strangler alpha (0.5.0): petri seed, unchanged at the CLI, runs the agentic decomposer end-to-end — organic trees, cross-colony edge rows, bedrock stops, a Y/n/edit prompt, overwrite refusal, and petri seed --resume. Claimed v2 surface is seed/check/graph/dashboard listing; grow arrives with M4-dbos and petri export with M6-storage.

issues.title: [EPIC] M4-dbos — Durable execution
issues.body:
> Milestone of the [Petri v2 migration tracker](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) (#100).

## Goal

Replace the hand-rolled durability layer (fcntl queue, busy-wait scheduler, load balancer, .stop sentinel) with DBOS durable execution behind the swappable ExecutionBackend seam (D1). The per-cell pipeline becomes a typed pydantic-graph run as DBOS workflows, execution state in a separate dbos.sqlite (D4); killed or rate-limited `petri grow`/`petri seed` resume with no re-paid LLM calls (D2), and `petri stop` becomes a durable cancel. Seed re-platform closes field report `#8`.

## Shipping

A minor release where `petri grow` runs each cell as an exactly-once durable workflow (keyed by cell key plus round) and `petri seed` keyed by colony id, resuming after kill/rate-limit/stop with no duplicate LLM spend or events. `petri.yaml` gains worker_concurrency and rate-limit settings, and the v1 engine is deleted per D8, removing the fcntl Windows blocker.

## Steps

- [ ] 1. #49 — Spike: validate DBOS-on-SQLite for durable execution *(start here; parallel with #50 and #51)*
- [ ] 2. #50 — Add an ExecutionBackend seam in front of the v1 engine *(parallel with #49 and #51)*
- [ ] 3. #51 — Make append_event idempotent with deterministic IDs *(parallel with #49/#50; needs M3 schema merged)*
- [ ] 4. #52 — Model the per-cell pipeline as a typed pydantic-graph *(after #50)*
- [ ] 5. #53 — Document the queue-state to pipeline-node mapping *(after #52; parallel with #54; good first issue)*
- [ ] 6. #54 — Port queue transition tests to graph conformance suite *(after #52; parallel with #53; gates #63)*
- [ ] 7. #55 — Port research-side phases into pipeline nodes *(after #51 and #52; parallel with #56)*
- [ ] 8. #56 — Port decision-side phases and iterate loop into nodes *(after #51 and #52; parallel with #55)*
- [ ] 9. #57 — Implement DBOSExecutionBackend with durable cell workflows *(needs #49 GO plus #50, #55, #56; longest item)*
- [ ] 10. #58 — Add grow_colony workflow for bottom-up scheduling *(after #57; parallel with #59, #60, #61)*
- [ ] 11. #59 — Re-platform petri seed onto the DBOS backend *(after #57; parallel with #58/#60/#61; closes report 8)*
- [ ] 12. #60 — Port sync-check as a startup reconciliation step *(after #57; parallel with #58, #59, #61)*
- [ ] 13. #61 — Repoint dashboard /api/queue onto the backend seam *(after #57; parallel with #58/#59/#60; needs #50)*
- [ ] 14. #62 — Rewire grow/stop/feed onto the durable backend *(after #58)*
- [ ] 15. #63 — Retire the v1 engine and fcntl queue *(last; needs #54 and #58 through #62)*

## Risks

- Failed spike is survivable: the seam allows a pydantic-graph FileStatePersistence fallback behind it.
- DBOS determinism fails silently: any filesystem/clock/config read in workflow code diverges on replay, so petri.sqlite reads must be steps.
- Steps are at-least-once; deterministic event IDs plus INSERT OR IGNORE guard duplicate spend, and the ID derivation must stay total.
- Cancellation preempts only at step boundaries, so `petri stop` cannot interrupt an in-flight LLM call; document the regression.
- append_event hardening depends on M3's petri.sqlite schema for the UNIQUE constraint; if it slips, both phase-port issues block.

issues.title: [EPIC] M5-otel — OpenTelemetry
issues.body:
> Milestone of the [Petri v2 migration tracker](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) (#100).

## Goal

OpenTelemetry becomes first-class across Petri: DBOS workflow/step spans, pydantic-ai agent/model spans, and petri.* domain attributes flow through one TracerProvider (D2, D7). The zero-infra default persists spans to petri.sqlite and renders per-cell waterfalls in petri launch; a telemetry: section adds OTLP export to self-hosted Jaeger, SigNoz, or Langfuse. Token and cost capture happens at the Model layer, since agents never self-report (docs/field-reports.md).

## Shipping

A v2 pre-release where every petri seed or grow run emits one end-to-end trace (CLI root, DBOS workflow/step, agent/model spans, all carrying petri.* attributes including verdict and cost) and petri launch shows per-cell waterfalls plus token/cost totals with nothing external running. A documented telemetry: section in petri.yaml points OTLP at any self-hosted backend.

## Steps

- [ ] 1. #64 — Add OTel bootstrap and petri.yaml telemetry section *(start here; parallel with #65)*
- [ ] 2. #65 — Spike: choose the pydantic-ai OTel instrumentation path *(start here; parallel with #64)*
- [ ] 3. #66 — Enable DBOS OTel spans behind the durability seam *(after #64; parallel with #67 and #69)*
- [ ] 4. #67 — Instrument pydantic-ai agent runs with OTel *(after #64 and #65; parallel with #66 and #69)*
- [ ] 5. #69 — Persist spans and usage rows to petri.sqlite *(after #64; parallel with #66 and #67)*
- [ ] 6. #68 — Attach petri.* domain attributes to spans *(after #66 and #67)*
- [ ] 7. #70 — Add read-only trace API endpoints to the dashboard *(after #69; parallel with #68)*
- [ ] 8. #71 — Add a per-cell trace waterfall to the dashboard *(after #70)*
- [ ] 9. #72 — Surface per-cell token and cost totals in the dashboard *(after #68 and #70; parallel with #71)*
- [ ] 10. #73 — Document observability: local default and OTLP export *(after #68; parallel with #71 and #72)*

## Risks

- pydantic-ai's OTel-native path is unverified; if the logfire SDK is required even in no-send mode, it becomes a pinned dependency.
- DBOS spans are example-verified mostly on Postgres; SQLite behavior and agent-span parenting under step spans may need explicit context propagation or links.
- petri grow writes spans while petri launch reads and prunes the same petri.sqlite; long exporter transactions risk stalls or 'database is locked'.
- Span volume (13 agents, 6 phases, 3 iterations, hundreds of cells) can bloat the spans table; sample_ratio/retention_days need tuning, and pruning must never touch events.
- Harness subprocesses stay opaque and subscription-auth backends may report no usage; the cost panel shows n/a, never fabricated zeros.

issues.title: [EPIC] M6-storage — Storage & dashboard reads
issues.body:
> Milestone of the [Petri v2 migration tracker](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) (#100).

## Goal

A typed petri/query layer over each dish's petri.sqlite (amended D4) replaces the JSONL-to-SQLite copy pipeline, and dashboard REST/SSE read it directly. ExecutionBackend-driven durable runs replace the PTY bridge and synchronous seeding. petri export makes text a git-reviewable artifact, petri backup snapshots paid compute via VACUUM INTO, and starter analytics views seed M7's Analyst.

## Shipping

petri launch boots with no event-index step and no combined.jsonl, every dashboard read comes from per-dish petri.sqlite via petri/query, and seeding enqueues a durable workflow. petri export regenerates deterministic text, and petri backup/--list/--restore work end to end on VACUUM INTO snapshots.

## Steps

- [ ] 1. #74 — Add a petri/query read layer over petri.sqlite *(start after M3 schema and dish layout)*
- [ ] 2. #82 — Harden colony graph integrity and persistence *(parallel with #74)*
- [ ] 3. #78 — Add petri backup with --list and a snapshot hook *(parallel with #74)*
- [ ] 4. #75 — Move REST endpoints to petri/query and add /api/edges *(after #74)*
- [ ] 5. #76 — Rebuild /api/stream on events-table tailing *(after #74; live channel waits on M2)*
- [ ] 6. #83 — Ship starter analytics views in petri.sqlite *(after #74, parallel with #75)*
- [ ] 7. #79 — Add petri backup --restore with an overwrite guard *(after #78)*
- [ ] 8. #80 — Add petri export for git-reviewable derived text *(after #74 and #78)*
- [ ] 9. #77 — Retire migrate.py and the disposable dashboard index *(after #75 and #76)*
- [ ] 10. #81 — Replace /api/proc and sync seed with durable runs *(last; needs M4 ExecutionBackend and durable seed)*

## Risks

- The events/cells/edges schema, write seam, dish layout, and user_version mechanism all land in M3-decomposer; the M6 query layer can't merge until they do.
- The integer watermark behind SSE tailing and export --since is safe only while events stays append-only; future pruning must target spans/usage, never events.
- SSE needs M2's event_stream_handler and /api/proc needs M4's ExecutionBackend plus durable seed; sequence both last, keep everything else landable on the v1 engine.
- Export determinism is load-bearing: M4 commits its golden grow fixture as exported text, so version the format in the manifest and coordinate changes.
- The analytics-views and M5 spans/usage migrations both bump user_version; agree numbering up front so the forward-only chain stays linear.

issues.title: [EPIC] M7-lifecycle — Iterative lifecycle
issues.body:
> Milestone of the [Petri v2 migration tracker](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) (#100).

## Goal

v1 dead-ends inconclusive, caveated, flawed, and stalled cells at their current granularity (field report `#9`). This milestone closes the loop: signal verdicts drive human-gated re-decomposition, petri feed forks instead of re-paying LLM steps, the scanner runs re-scoped on cron, cross-colony edges become ranking intelligence, and a read-only Analyst watches research health. Seed foundation colonies first, since search_cells can only reference existing cells.

## Shipping

A v2.x release: the four signal verdicts produce human-approved re-decomposition proposals via petri grow --redecompose-on, petri feed re-validates by forking and raises typed ingest errors, petri scan runs on cron, check/graph/dashboard rank cells by edge intelligence with opt-in scheduler priority, and the Analyst surfaces health flags.

## Steps

- [ ] 1. #84 — Write the verdict-driven re-decomposition RFC *(start here; anchors the re-decomposition track)*
- [ ] 2. #90 — Extend the edge registry with dish-level graph queries *(parallel with #84)*
- [ ] 3. #88 — Re-validate fed evidence by forking workflows *(parallel with #84)*
- [ ] 4. #89 — Re-scope the contradiction scanner and schedule it *(parallel with #84)*
- [ ] 5. #95 — Write the GitHub feedback re-entry RFC *(parallel; docs only)*
- [ ] 6. #96 — Archive merged worktrees and record corpus provenance *(parallel; no source changes)*
- [ ] 7. #85 — Detect re-decomposition triggers from verdict history *(after #84)*
- [ ] 8. #91 — Compute edge-intelligence metrics from the dish graph *(after #90; good first issue)*
- [ ] 9. #86 — Build the re-decomposition proposal workflow *(after #85)*
- [ ] 10. #92 — Surface edge intelligence in CLI and dashboard *(after #90 and #91)*
- [ ] 11. #93 — Add opt-in convergence-point priority to grow scheduling *(after #91; parallel with #92)*
- [ ] 12. #94 — Add a read-only Analyst for research-health flags *(after #91)*
- [ ] 13. #87 — Add the re-decomposition approval gate to petri grow *(after #86; completes the loop)*

## Risks

- No real grow runs exist yet, so every lifecycle design extrapolates from seeding; RFC-first issues and opt-in flags hold until the first v2 grow validates them.
- Loop explosion: a field run inflated 101 claims to 983 cells (9.7x) at 13 agents each, so hard caps, bedrock stops, and the human gate are mandatory; auto-approve ships off.
- DBOS uncertainty (D1 keeps it behind a seam): fork_workflow start_step on SQLite is undocumented, forked runs get new workflow_ids breaking workflow_id==cell-key, and create_schedule must register before launch; the feed issue carries a fallback.
- Scanner scope shrinks as M2-agents and M4-dbos delete categories; re-inventory before porting, and M4 only disables queue-dependent checks.
- Priority swaps stay enqueue-time only, since DBOS code-checksum versioning strands in-flight workflows; edge-intelligence full recomputes are unmeasured at 983-cell scale and may need caching.

issues.title: Create petri/harness error taxonomy and retry core
issues.body:
> [v2 migration #100](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) › **M1-harness** ([epic #9](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/9)) · Size **S** · [Architecture](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md)

## Goal

New petri/harness package: the typed error vocabulary and configurable backoff policy every v2 backend shares, respecting rate-limit reset hints.

## Context

Both new backends need one failure vocabulary; today it lives inline in claude_code_provider.py:33-81, where stderr-only classification let a rate limit (empty stderr, reset hint on stdout) burn all retries. v2 is fail-loud: malformed output becomes a typed error, never coerced.

## Scope

**In:**

- petri/harness/errors.py: HarnessError base + JSON-serializable FailureDetail (exit_code, stderr_tail, stdout_tail, last_stream_event, partial_output) fitting the event data field.
- Subclasses: TransientHarnessError, PermanentHarnessError, RateLimitedError(Transient) with retry_after_seconds, AuthExpiredError(Permanent) with an actionable message.
- petri/harness/retry.py: RetryPolicy (max_retries, base, cap, jitter) + pure delay function, configurable to zero retries.
- Policy honors retry_after_seconds (reset beyond cap surfaces immediately); parse_reset_hint reads relative and clock forms, clock injectable.
- Pluggable per-backend classification over exit code, stderr AND stdout, permanent-wins precedence; add pydantic-ai>=2.9,<3 to pyproject.toml core deps.

**Out:**

- No transports or Model subclasses; own issues
- No changes under petri/reasoning/ or its tests

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] uv run pytest tests/unit/harness/ passes with no network, no claude CLI, no pi; import pydantic_ai succeeds after install.
- [ ] Retry-delay test: exponential base growth, bounded jitter, cap respected; max_retries=0 performs exactly one attempt.
- [ ] Classification reads stdout: exit 1 + empty stderr + stdout 'resets 9pm (America/Los_Angeles)' yields RateLimitedError with retry_after_seconds; permanent-wins precedence holds.
- [ ] parse_reset_hint returns N*60 for 'try again in N minutes', seconds-until-next-9pm under a frozen clock, None otherwise.
- [ ] A RateLimitedError whose retry_after_seconds exceeds the cap surfaces immediately, no further attempts (v1 burned three retries in ~5s).
- [ ] FailureDetail round-trips through JSON and fits the event envelope data field; git diff zero under petri/reasoning/ and test_claude_code_provider.py; suite green.

## Pointers

- petri/reasoning/claude_code_provider.py:28,33-81: inline logic generalized (read-only)
- tests/unit/test_claude_code_provider.py:336-514: precedence pin, stays green
- docs/field-reports.md: rate-limit and silent-PASS evidence
- New: petri/harness/{errors,retry}.py, tests/unit/harness/test_{errors,retry}.py

---
`#N` in this issue refers to entries in [docs/field-reports.md](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/field-reports.md), not issues in this repo.

issues.body:
> [v2 migration #100](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) › **M1-harness** ([epic #9](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/9)) · Size **S** · [Architecture](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md)

## Goal

PiRpcTransport spawns pi --mode rpc, frames LF-delimited JSONL both ways, manages a long-lived session, and maps every failure into the petri/harness taxonomy.

## Context

This replaces, for pi, the subprocess plumbing v1 hand-rolls at claude_code_provider.py:327-506; the protocol comes from docs/spikes/pi-rpc.md. Fail-loud throughout: a malformed frame raises a typed HarnessError, never coerced or partially parsed.

## Scope

**In:**

- petri/harness/pi/transport.py: binary discovery (PETRI_PI_BIN, then shutil.which('pi')), spawn pi --mode rpc with configured --provider/model/tool flags.
- Strict LF framing both directions; per-request timeout (default 300s, configurable); graceful shutdown and kill-on-timeout.
- One in-flight request per transport, lock-serialized unless the spike proved multiplexing.
- Map stderr/stdout/in-band payloads to Transient/Permanent/RateLimited; malformed frames raise a typed HarnessError carrying the raw line in FailureDetail.
- Detect mid-request death, raise, restart the session next use; test vs fake_pi plus one real-pi round-trip.

**Out:**

- No pydantic-ai Model mapping (PiModel issue); no engine/reasoning changes
- No fork/resume beyond reuse; no retry orchestration (callers apply RetryPolicy)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All transport unit tests run offline against fake_pi; the integration test completes one real round-trip and auto-skips without pi on PATH.
- [ ] Framing test: a response with embedded \n and \r\n in JSON string fields round-trips intact, no CRLF/LF ambiguity.
- [ ] Timeout test: a slow fake_pi response raises within the configured timeout and the process is reaped (returncode/poll).
- [ ] Concurrent calls on one transport serialize through the lock, or multiplex if the spike proved it (cite the transcript).
- [ ] Injected transient/permanent/rate-limit yield Transient/Permanent/RateLimitedError (retry_after when hint present); no path returns coerced or partial text.
- [ ] Malformed frame (non-JSON, truncated) raises a typed HarnessError carrying the raw line; mid-request death raises then restarts the session; spike-doc unknowns updated; suite green.

## Context

The decision record locks convergence as a boolean verdict-set check with no LLM, to preserve exactly. Today it runs on YAML-loaded roles with a string-blocking hack, a bare-str outcome (models.py:400-405), YAML-order-dependent weakest-link, and a redundant short-circuit recompute.

**In:**

- Exact convergence semantics: last-write-wins per agent, leads excluded, conditional agents vote with redirect on block, converged iff all blocking/conditional pass and none missing
- Weakest-link missing-outranks-failing; short-circuit fires only on a matching verdict with all other blocking passing and none missing; circuit breaker stays relative counting (iteration - cycle_start >= max_iterations), field-validated
- EXECUTION_ERROR (M1-harness fail-loud): exhausted-retry failures become an explicit events-table verdict counting against convergence, never satisfying it
- Determinism fix: weakest-link order = AgentName definition order, not YAML dict order; noted in ADR and release notes

- [ ] EXECUTION_ERROR counts against convergence and never satisfies it: a cell with all other blocking passing plus one EXECUTION_ERROR does not converge; it is absent from every pass set and ranks as failing, not missing
- [ ] Weakest-link selection is deterministic under dict-key shuffling of the input verdicts (test permutes insertion order)

## Context

- [ ] --model overrides the config model (injected resolver); an unknown agent exits non-zero listing valid AgentName values

issues.body:
> [v2 migration #100](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) › **M3-decomposer** ([epic #11](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/11)) · Size **S** · [Architecture](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md)

## Goal

A per-dish petri.sqlite becomes the domain source of truth: append-only events, cells and edges tables, and a forward-only migration mechanism.

## Context

Amended D4: one Petri-owned SQLite file per dish (stdlib sqlite3 only) replaces per-cell JSONL, metadata.json mutations, and evidence.md stubs, with a separate dbos.sqlite for M4-dbos. Append-only is schema-enforced; text becomes a derived export artifact.

## Scope

**In:**

- petri/storage/database.py: connect(db_path) applying PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout, and user_version forward-only migrations
- Migration runner over an ordered script list (petri/storage/migrations/), one transaction per script, user_version bumped on success; fail loud on a future version
- Schema v1 events: deterministic UNIQUE TEXT id, cell_id, event_type, JSON payload, created_at NOT NULL; idempotent INSERT OR IGNORE; UPDATE/DELETE triggers raise
- cells (id PK, colony, level, seq, claim_text, status, relation, is_atomic, bedrock_reason, created_at NOT NULL CHECK<>''); edges (from/to_cell, edge_type, reason, created_at); dependents VIEW
- append_event and read functions on database.py as the single write seam; event_log.py append/read re-pointed as thin wrappers; documented stable event-id derivation

**Out:**

- spans/usage (M5-otel), seed_checkpoints (resume issue), petri/query and export (M6-storage)

- [ ] Integration: a fixture DAG (cells, edges, events) round-trips across close/reopen and the dependents view answers correctly
- [ ] pytest: connect() on a fresh path creates petri.sqlite at WAL and current user_version; reopening applies no migrations; a FUTURE version fails loudly naming both
- [ ] pytest: a failing migration leaves user_version unchanged (one transaction per script)
- [ ] pytest: a duplicate event id yields one row (INSERT OR IGNORE, reported duplicate); UPDATE/DELETE on events raises; the seam exposes no event update/delete API
- [ ] pytest: a cell with NULL/'' created_at fails the CHECK; event-id derivation is identical across processes (stable-hash)

## Goal

## Context

Field reports `#10` (243 of 983 cells were trivial axioms, each burning the 13-agent pipeline), `#13` (only supporting children), and `#12` (no negative examples yields unfalsifiable claims); a fourth failure is restatement children. All fixes validated in a 148-cell re-seed.

**In:**

- relation: Literal['supports','limits','rebuts'] on PremiseCandidate (replaces placeholder) and Cell (models.py:263-274, default 'supports'), persisted as a cells-table column via decomposer.py:379-408

## Goal

The seed approval prompt gains an edit choice, so one wrong sub-claim no longer forces accepting the flaw or re-paying full regeneration.

## Context

The original CLI specified Y/n/edit but the shipped prompt offers only whole-tree accept/regenerate/abort (seed.py ~390-472). The typed per-node results from the pydantic-ai rebuild make an edit path safe: edits re-validate through the agents' own schemas.

## Scope

**In:**

- An 'edit' choice in the seed approval prompt alongside accept/regenerate/abort
- Editing mechanics: dump pending sub-claims as YAML into $EDITOR; inline fallback (edit N <text>, drop N, done); rewrite text, delete, change relation, or mark atomic
- On save, re-validate the edited block through the SAME pydantic schemas the agents use; invalid edits re-prompt with the error, not crash or silently accept
- Audit trail: a decomposition_edited event (original + edited text) through the registry, appended to the events table (amended D4)

**Out:**

- Editing already-persisted cells (M7-lifecycle re-decomposition)

- [ ] pytest (scripted editor): editing one sub-claim's text yields a created cell with that text, and a decomposition_edited event records original and edited text
- [ ] pytest: drop N removes exactly that sub-claim; the remaining sub-claims are created unchanged
- [ ] pytest: an edit producing schema-invalid YAML (e.g. unknown relation) re-prompts with the validation error and creates no cells
- [ ] pytest: edited output still passes per-parent cap truncation and the near-duplication guard (an edit duplicating the parent is rejected like model output)
- [ ] Manual smoke (documented in PR): the session shows the edit option, the $EDITOR round-trip works, and accept-without-edit behaves as before

issues.body:

## Goal

Decomposition quality becomes measured: fixture claims, a ground-truth graph, and seven evaluators guard the known failure modes.

## Context

D6 mandates the suite. Four prompt iterations on one root claim (indexed in docs/field-reports.md) produced the record the evaluators encode: v1 quota phrasing filled every level, v3 inverse bias tunneled into binary splits, v4 neutral phrasing gave organic counts.

## Scope

**In:**

- Eval corpus under evals/decomposer/: claims.yaml (v1-v4 root claim family, axiom-heavy claim, contested claim, two-colony reference-rate dish) and fixtures/ (claims-graph.json ground truth: 88 nodes/128 edges/60 cross-layer, acyclic; archive 4-13 layer distribution; ~7 paired-wave A/B decompositions; principle-vs-measurement splits 08-04a/b, 08-07a/b, 08-09a/b)
- Negative Cases scoring POORLY: the hotdog-sandwich template output (5 generic subclaims) and the v0.1.0 _default_decompose hardcoded template children
- evaluators.py/dataset.py with seven evaluators over DecompositionResult: NoQuotaFill (>=2 consecutive levels at ceiling), OrganicVariation (per-level vs 4-13 AND L1 varies with complexity), CounterargumentPresence (fraction of parents with limits/rebuts above threshold), BedrockStop (axiom terminates is_atomic within depth 2, trivial rate <25%), CrossColonyReferenceRate (second colony yields >=1 edge on the matching cell, not root), DepthOrganic (depth varies), ParentChildDistinctness (no child near-duplicates parent)
- Offline mode: evaluators over FunctionModel-scripted end-to-end decompositions, deterministic, zero network, wired into uv run pytest via tests/evals/test_decomposer_evals.py; live mode gated behind PETRI_LIVE_EVALS=1 and a marker, never CI; README documents live cost and offline-by-default
- Deliberate-regression check: reinstating quota phrasing ('Pick the TOP N') fails the instruction-content assertions and NoQuotaFill. Optional stretch (separate commit, droppable): advisory LLMJudge scoring falsifiability on a cheap model, never gating

**Out:**

- Grow-phase verdict evals (M2-agents)
- Logfire/OTel upload of results (M5-otel, D7)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The offline suite is part of uv run pytest tests/, runs green over FunctionModel-scripted end-to-end decompositions with zero network/subprocess, and adds under 30s
- [ ] pytest: all fixtures load and validate (claims-graph.json parses, is acyclic, matches 88/128/60); each negative fixture is documented in-repo with its failure mode
- [ ] pytest offline: NoQuotaFill fails a v1-shaped result and passes a v4-organic one; OrganicVariation fails uniform-L1 and passes L1-varies-with-complexity; ParentChildDistinctness fails a restatement child
- [ ] pytest offline: the hotdog-sandwich and v0.1.0 negative fixtures score poorly on the relevant evaluators; the search_cells precision/recall Case runs against claims-graph.json and reports numbers
- [ ] Live (PETRI_LIVE_EVALS=1 ... -m live, verified once in the PR): executes the Dataset against the configured model, the two-colony Case yields >=1 cross-colony reference edge, and prints a per-case/per-evaluator report
- [ ] README documents the live-eval cost and offline-by-default policy; the deliberate-regression check demonstrably fails when quota phrasing is reinstated (shown once in the PR)

## Goal

Prove or disprove DBOS on SQLite before any backend code, producing measured numbers, committed fixtures, and a GO/NO-GO ADR.

## Context

D1 bars Petri from requiring Docker or Postgres, so DBOS must earn its place on SQLite first. Findings gate M3's interim SeedCheckpointStore design and every downstream backend decision.

**In:**

- Throwaway spikes/dbos-sqlite/ (excluded from wheel): crash-resume, idempotency, queue concurrency, rate limiting, polling latency, volume, fork, cancel, pickle limits

**Out:**

- Any change to petri/ production code

- [ ] kill -9 mid-step then relaunch runs each completed step exactly once and PENDING workflows to completion; SetWorkflowID twice executes once and deduplication_id raises DBOSQueueDeduplicatedError

issues.title: Make append_event idempotent with deterministic IDs
issues.body:
> [v2 migration #100](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) › **M4-dbos** ([epic #12](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/12)) · Size **S** · [Architecture](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md)

## Goal

Derive event IDs deterministically and make appends INSERT OR IGNORE on the events table's UNIQUE constraint, so retries never double-write.

## Context

Imported from M6-storage; at-least-once steps make it load-bearing. Today append_event uses random token_hex IDs and a full-file collision scan (event_log.py:27-73); amended D4 ships the UNIQUE constraint in M3, leaving this issue derivation plus INSERT OR IGNORE.

## Scope

**In:**

- Deterministic IDs from (cell_id, round, node, agent, iteration) plus a type/sequence discriminator; documented and total
- Appends via INSERT OR IGNORE on the UNIQUE event-id constraint; a duplicate ID returns the existing event, no-op
- No presence index or log rescan; the DB constraint is the only idempotency mechanism
- event_log.py stays the single writer; rows not lines, append-only, envelope {id,cell_id,timestamp,type,agent,iteration,data} unchanged
- No migration tooling; v2 starts fresh per D8

**Out:**

- The events/cells/edges schema and PRAGMA migration (M3's schema issue)
- Phase runners (phase-port issues) and DBOS; pure storage-layer hardening

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Appending the same logical event twice (identical cell_id/round/node/agent/iteration plus discriminator) yields one row; the second call is a no-op returning the existing event
- [ ] Two independent processes compute the same ID for the same inputs with no coordination
- [ ] A retry-storm test (same event appended 50 times, including concurrently) produces one row and a queryable, uncorrupted events table
- [ ] The envelope {id,cell_id,timestamp,type,agent,iteration,data} is preserved and validate_event_data passes on all written events
- [ ] Idempotency comes from INSERT OR IGNORE on the UNIQUE constraint; no application-level presence scan or ID index exists (test or grep)
- [ ] No third-party storage dependency; all writes use stdlib sqlite3 through the single write seam

## Goal

A DBOS ExecutionBackend runs each validation round as a durable, exactly-once workflow with crash-resume, queue flow control, and rate-limit sleep on SQLite.

## Context

Gated on a GO from the DBOS-on-SQLite spike. One workflow validate_cell(cell_id, round) runs the pydantic-graph with phase functions wrapped @DBOS.step; SetWorkflowID(f"{cell_key}:r{round}") gives exactly-once identity per round (D2.3, build_cell_key at models.py:512-514).

## Scope

**In:**

- NEW petri/execution/dbos_backend.py and dbos_app.py
- App bootstrap, queue config from petri.yaml, execution.backend: dbos opt-in flag
- validate_cell durable workflow with exactly-once round identity
- Rate-limit durable sleep, throttling policy, startup resource report
- Crash-resume and exactly-once integration tests

**Out:**

- Colony orchestration, stop/resume/feed, seed workflow, v1 deletion (separate issues)
- Postgres/Conductor/Console (never bundled); OTLP config (M5, leave hook)

- [ ] execution.backend=dbos validates a single cell end-to-end on the diamond fixture (FakeProvider/TestModel), creating dbos.sqlite under .petri/ separate from petri.sqlite, no Docker/Postgres; v1 stays default until retire-v1

## Goal

## Context

DBOS has no DAG engine and the colony DAG stays data, so bottom-up scheduling stays Petri logic in a durable parent workflow. It loads ColonyGraph from petri.sqlite (amended D4), keeps get_eligible_for_validation (colony.py:212-238) as-is, and orchestrates children on the DBOS queue.

**In:**

**Out:**

> [v2 migration #100](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) › **M4-dbos** ([epic #12](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/12)) · Size **S** · [Architecture](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md)

## Goal

At `petri grow` startup, detect divergence between petri.sqlite domain state and DBOS execution state and park divergent cells for human resolution.

## Context

petri.sqlite and dbos.sqlite can diverge (crash between event append and checkpoint, or a restored backup mid-run); v1 archives hit this three times. v1's sync_check (queue.py:285-383) parked such cells, and retire-v1 deletes it, so this carries the capability forward.

**In:**

- A DBOS-backend reconciliation step at `petri grow` startup comparing cells/events tables against DBOS workflow status per cell

- Surface parked conflicts in `petri check` with the divergence reason

**Out:**

- [ ] Replacing petri.sqlite with an older snapshot mid-run makes the next `petri grow` startup park affected cells in sync_conflict rather than crash or re-run them
- [ ] A cell whose DBOS workflow reports SUCCESS but whose cells-table row lacks a terminal status is detected as divergent and parked
- [ ] Reconciliation never modifies the events table (row count and content hash asserted before/after; append-only preserved)
- [ ] `petri check` lists parked sync-conflict cells with a human-readable divergence reason

issues.body:
> [v2 migration #100](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) › **M5-otel** ([epic #13](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/13)) · Size **S** · [Architecture](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md)

## Goal

A zero-infra local span sink: an OTel exporter writes spans and usage rows to petri.sqlite tables, age-pruned, readable via one query API.

## Context

D7's zero-infra requirement means traces show in petri launch with nothing external running. Amended D4 (docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md): petri.sqlite holds domain tables plus these two telemetry tables, stdlib sqlite3 only, on M3-decomposer's PRAGMA user_version migration and WAL mode.

## Scope

**In:**

- Forward-only migration adding spans and usage tables to petri.sqlite (stdlib sqlite3 only; no DuckDB).
- spans columns: trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, name, kind, start/end_time_ns, status_code, status_message, attributes (JSON), resource (JSON).
- usage columns (one per usage-bearing span): span_id, trace_id, cell_id, phase, agent_role, tokens_input, tokens_output, cost_usd (nullable).
- petri/telemetry/span_store.py exporter registered when telemetry.local.enabled (default true); extracts usage from petri.tokens_input/output/cost_usd (no usage attrs, no row); never raises into pipeline (locked DB drops spans, warns once); busy_timeout + short per-batch transactions.
- query_spans(petri_dir, cell_id, trace_id, limit) typed rows; prune() removes rows older than retention_days on petri launch startup (near launch.py:171-173).

**Out:**

- No dashboard endpoints/UI (#70) or remote OTLP export (#64).
- Never writes the append-only events table; not petri export (M6-storage).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] pytest: exporting 100 synthetic spans then reading via query_spans returns 100 rows with trace_id/span_id/parent_span_id intact and petri.* attributes JSON round-tripped; query_spans(cell_id=...) filters via petri.cell_id.
- [ ] pytest: the migration applies cleanly at the prior user_version, bumps it, is a no-op on re-open; usage aggregates per cell and per phase via plain SQL (indexed columns present).
- [ ] pytest: spans with petri.tokens_input/output produce matching usage rows; spans without produce none (no zero-filled rows).
- [ ] pytest: the exporter against a read-only/locked DB warns once and does not raise; it commits in per-batch transactions (no transaction outlives a batch); the PR documents the transaction/busy_timeout strategy.
- [ ] pytest: one process exports while another reads via query_spans (multiprocessing, WAL mode); all committed spans read back without corruption or unhandled 'database is locked'.
- [ ] pytest: prune() removes rows older than retention_days and keeps newer ones; everything writes only inside the dish's petri.sqlite (stdlib sqlite3, no network) and events/cells/edges contents are identical before and after export, prune, and migration.

issues.body:
> [v2 migration #100](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) › **M6-storage** ([epic #14](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/14)) · Size **S** · [Architecture](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md)

## Goal

petri export regenerates deterministic JSONL/markdown from petri.sqlite so dishes are git-committable and greppable, with text never a second source of truth.

## Context

Under amended D4 the database is the domain source of truth and text is derived. Determinism is load-bearing: M4-dbos commits its golden grow fixture as exported text, so identical DB state must always produce an identical tree.

## Scope

**In:**

- New petri/cli/export.py (register(app) pattern); all reads via petri/query, read-only; output under exports/, excluded from enumeration.
- Scopes: petri export (whole dish), --colony <slug>, --cell <cell_id>.
- Per-cell events.jsonl (one event/line, append order) and markdown (claim, status, level, dependencies, verdict, evidence/summary), plus dish-level edges.jsonl.
- Deterministic: append-order key, stable JSON key order and file iteration, trailing newlines; same DB state -> byte-identical tree.
- --since <watermark> rewrites only changed cells and updates a manifest (watermark + format version); petri grow --export / petri.yaml flag and backup --with-export trigger incremental runs.

**Out:**

- Importing exports back into petri.sqlite (D8)

## Goal

Remove the /api/proc PTY bridge, make seeding enqueue-only against the ExecutionBackend, and add proper run-control endpoints.

## Context

The dashboard violates D1/D4 twice: /api/proc spawns unreaped PTY subprocesses in an in-process _proc table, and POST /api/seed (api.py:490) runs decomposition synchronously, so a dropped connection leaves a half-written colony. M4-dbos ships the seam this moves onto.

**In:**

- Remove the /api/proc PTY bridge endpoints and the in-process _proc session table; reap live session state cleanly on shutdown during the transition.
- POST /api/seed validates input, starts the durable seed workflow via ExecutionBackend (workflow id = colony id), returns 202 with id and status URL; zero domain writes in-request.
- Re-seeding an existing colony still calls snapshot_before_destructive before overwrite (at enqueue or as the workflow's first step; test either way).

issues.body:
> [v2 migration #100](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) › **M6-storage** ([epic #14](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/14)) · Size **S** · [Architecture](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md)

## Goal

One authoritative in-memory colony topology, validated and deduped edges, and lossless save/load over the cells/edges tables, preserving the cross-colony edges v1 dropped.

## Context

Topology lives twice with nothing forcing agreement: Cell.dependencies/dependents (models.py) and ColonyGraph's _adj/_rev (colony.py). v1's defects must not carry over: add_edge never validated or deduped, serialize dropped cross-colony edges (field report `#11`), load_colonies (_bootstrap.py:57-72) silently skipped failures.

## Scope

**In:**

- One authoritative representation; Cell.dependencies/dependents derived from it; module docstring documents the choice and invariant.
- add_edge validates both local endpoints exist and dedupes in memory; cross-colony endpoints validated against the edge_registry row shape and preserved as typed references.
- remove_cell keeps both in-memory views and the cells/edges rows consistent, leaving no dangling ids; the dependents view reflects removal.
- Save/load via M3's write seam, lossless including cross-colony edges (save-load-save is a fixpoint); dedupe belt-and-braces (in-memory plus edges UNIQUE).
- The loader surfaces invalid data (edge to a missing cell, model-validation failure) with dish and colony named, and continues loading healthy colonies.

**Out:**

- petri/query read layer; schema and edge registry (M3)
- Cross-colony DishGraph queries and cycle detection (M7)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] pytest: save-load-save over cells/edges is a fixpoint for a fixture with a cross-colony edge; Cell lists and ColonyGraph adjacency agree after the round trip (stable ordering, edge preserved).
- [ ] pytest: add_edge with a nonexistent local endpoint raises a typed error; adding the same edge twice yields one in-memory edge and one edges-table row (UNIQUE-backed).
- [ ] pytest: after remove_cell and a round trip, neither in-memory view nor the cells/edges tables hold a dangling reference and the dependents view reflects removal.
- [ ] pytest: Cell lists agree with ColonyGraph adjacency after an arbitrary add_edge/remove_cell sequence (property-style).
- [ ] pytest: loading a dish with one colony's invalid edge row reports that colony by id and still loads the healthy ones (no silent skip).
- [ ] Full test suite passes with the rewritten colony/graph tests.

## Goal

Turn a RedecompositionTrigger into a persisted proposal: a DBOS workflow runs the M3 decomposer, inserts proposed sub-claims, and appends a redecomposition_proposed event.

## Context

Executes the second half of field report `#9`: in v1 decompose_why runs only during seeding, and the circuit-breaker path only audits and stops (processor.py:1009), so this workflow supersedes it. Verdict-context prompt framing stays provisional until grow evidence.

## Scope

**In:**

- New petri/lifecycle/redecompose.py: workflow consuming RedecompositionTrigger, decompose_why as a checkpointed step, typed DecompositionResult validation.
- Insert proposed cells and edges into the colony graph, recompute levels (compute_levels), persist cells via the v2 storage path.
- Append a redecomposition_proposed domain event with its payload model registered in EVENT_DATA_MODELS.
- Guards from petri.yaml keys: max rounds/cell, per-parent cap with hard truncation, bedrock stop, dish budget.
- Evidence by path only (pickle <2MB); spans carry petri.* attributes (M5-otel). Tests: test_redecompose.py plus a FunctionModel integration test.

**Out:**

- No human gate, --redecompose-on flags, or enqueueing (next issue).

- [ ] Integration (FunctionModel): a cell driven to EVIDENCE_INCONCLUSIVE emits a redecomposition_proposed event with a registered schema-valid payload, and its proposed sub-claims and edges land in the colony graph pointing at the triggering cell, levels recomputed and cells persisted via the v2 storage path.
- [ ] No code path enqueues a validation workflow; the output is a proposal only, and convergence.py stays untouched.
- [ ] Killing the process mid-re-decomposition and restarting resumes with no duplicate proposals or double-paid decomposer calls (DBOS checkpointing plus deterministic workflow id, asserted via list_workflow_steps).
- [ ] CRITICAL_FLAW_FOUND yields at least one counterargument-framed sub-claim; invalid decomposer output raises ModelRetry, not a crash or silent empty result (FunctionModel test).
- [ ] Checkpointed step inputs contain evidence paths only, no bodies; spans carry the petri.* attribute set.

**In:**

- petri/lifecycle/revalidate.py: cell-to-workflow mapping, fork point = first research step, DBOS.fork_workflow call.

> [v2 migration #100](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) › **M7-lifecycle** ([epic #15](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/15)) · Size **S** · [Architecture](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md)

## Goal

When enabled, grow schedules convergence-point cells first; off by default, where M4-dbos's level-derived priority applies unchanged.

## Context

M4-dbos ships the grow queue with priority_enabled=True and level-derived priority as default; this replaces that ordering when enabled and falls back to it, not FIFO. DBOS accepts a per-enqueue priority; whether it helps throughput is a grow-only question, so ship opt-in.

## Scope

**In:**

- At the grow fan-out (successor of get_eligible_for_validation, colony.py:212-238), compute EdgeIntelligenceReport once per pass; priority = convergence points by rank, then importance, ties by level.
- Priority never overrides dependency eligibility (the fan-out predicate enforces it).
- Opt-in petri.yaml key (scheduling.prioritize_targets, default false).
- Enqueue-time only, no workflow-code changes, so DBOS code-checksum versioning and in-flight workflows are unaffected.
- Record assigned priority as an OTel span attribute and in the cell's queued domain event.

**Out:**

- No adaptive rate-limit-aware priority (D2, M4-dbos).
- No starvation protection beyond the tie-break; no eligibility or queue-declaration changes.

- [ ] Flag on, concurrency=1: a convergence-point cell enqueued alongside a same-level leaf executes first (integration, TestModel).
- [ ] Flag off (default): assigned priorities equal M4-dbos's level-derived ordering (regression asserting priority values, not FIFO).
- [ ] Priority never schedules a cell with unvalidated dependencies (eligibility test with priority enabled).
- [ ] Assigned priority appears in the cell's queued domain event and as a span attribute.
- [ ] Docs cover the key and default and state that enabling it replaces M4-dbos's level-derived priority.
- [ ] The diff contains no workflow-code changes (enqueue-time only).

issues.title: Petri v2 migration — master tracker
issues.body:
## Architecture at a glance

**Before** — `petri-grow` v0.3.4, the hand-rolled runtime:

![Petri v0.3.4 hand-rolled runtime: the CLI drives a grow loop, processor, fcntl queue, and load balancer; a ~900-line provider shells out to the Claude Code CLI; JSONL logs feed a disposable SQLite index for the dashboard.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/onthemarkdata/petri/main/docs/v2/images/architecture-before.jpeg)

**After** — Petri v2, typed agents on a durable substrate:

![Petri v2 target: the unchanged CLI drives a colony workflow and DBOS queue behind an ExecutionBackend seam; a pydantic-graph per-cell pipeline runs typed agents through a pi-default harness; all domain data lives in one petri.sqlite per dish, with text exported as a derived artifact.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/onthemarkdata/petri/main/docs/v2/images/architecture-after.jpeg)

*(Full decision record and module fates: [docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md).)*

## What this is

Petri v2 re-platforms the engine while keeping the CLI, the colony model, and the zero-infrastructure design intact. Two problems from real dogfood use drive it. First, the breakdown logic is template-driven: one run produced 983 cells against a 101-claim hand-crafted baseline, roughly a quarter of them trivially-true. Second, the runtime hand-rolls distributed-systems plumbing (a 14-state fcntl-locked queue, an adaptive load balancer, a subprocess stream parser, and an external bash retry wrapper), and a rate-limit interrupt once destroyed an 88-cell colony worth of paid compute.

v2 moves the workflow onto typed agents (Pydantic AI), a typed per-cell pipeline (pydantic-graph), durable execution behind a swappable seam (DBOS on its SQLite default), a pi-default harness with Claude Code kept as a backend, OpenTelemetry throughout, and one Petri-owned `petri.sqlite` per dish as the domain store. No Docker, no Postgres.

## Milestones

Each milestone is a tracking epic with its own scoped, claimable task issues. Rough order below; the epics carry the exact dependencies.

- [ ] #9 — **M1-harness**: backend-selectable inference; pi default, Claude Code kept
- [ ] #10 — **M2-agents**: 13-agent roster as typed agents; real debates; mechanical convergence preserved
- [ ] #11 — **M3-decomposer**: search_cells, bedrock stop, per-parent caps, and a pydantic_evals regression suite
- [ ] #12 — **M4-dbos**: per-cell pipeline as durable DBOS workflows on SQLite; crash-resume, exactly-once
- [ ] #13 — **M5-otel**: OTLP export plus an in-dashboard trace waterfall from a local spans table
- [ ] #14 — **M6-storage**: one petri.sqlite per dish; petri export; DuckDB dropped; migrate.py retired
- [ ] #15 — **M7-lifecycle**: verdict-driven re-decomposition, feed/fork re-validation, the Analyst

## Where to start

Two spikes gate everything and run in parallel:

- **#17** — validate `pi --mode rpc` end to end (in #9)
- **#49** — validate DBOS-on-SQLite for durable execution (in #12)

New here? Filter for [good first issues](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/../../issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22), then read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Comment on an issue to claim it.

issues.title: Wire `petri --version` into the CLI
issues.body:
## Goal

`petri --version` prints the installed version and exits, so users (and bug reports) can confirm which version they are running.

## Context

`petri.__version__` already resolves the installed version from package metadata (via setuptools-scm), but the Typer app has no `--version` flag, so there is no way to check the version from the command line. The bug-report template asks reporters for their version; a `--version` flag makes that a one-liner.

## Scope

- In: a top-level `--version` option on the `petri` app that prints the version and exits.
- Out: per-subcommand version flags, and a separate `petri version` subcommand (a flag is enough).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `petri --version` prints the version (for example `petri 0.3.7`) and exits 0 without running any command.
- [ ] The printed value matches `petri.__version__` (i.e. `importlib.metadata.version("petri-grow")`).
- [ ] It is eager and works with no subcommand, so it does not require a valid `.petri/` project on disk.
- [ ] A test covers it (Typer's `CliRunner`, asserting the output contains the version), kept offline like the rest of the suite.

## Pointers

- The Typer app is created in `petri/cli/__init__.py` (`app = typer.Typer(...)`, around line 24). Add an `@app.callback()` with a `--version` `typer.Option(..., is_eager=True, callback=...)` that prints `petri.__version__` and raises `typer.Exit()`. Standard Typer pattern:
  ```python
  def _version_callback(value: bool) -> None:
      if value:
          from petri import __version__
          typer.echo(f"petri {__version__}")
          raise typer.Exit()

  @app.callback()
  def main(
      version: bool = typer.Option(
          None, "--version", callback=_version_callback, is_eager=True,
          help="Show the Petri version and exit.",
      ),
  ) -> None:
      ...
  ```
- Version source: `petri/__init__.py` exposes `__version__` (reads installed metadata). Import it lazily inside the callback.
- Tests: `tests/integration/test_cli.py` already drives the app with Typer's `CliRunner`; add a case there. The suite is offline (mock at the provider seam), and this flag needs no inference, so it should stay trivially offline.

issues.title: Wire up the pi harness end-to-end
issues.body:
> [v2 migration #100](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/100) › **M1-harness** ([epic #9](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/issues/9)) · Tracking issue · [Architecture](https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-V2.md)

## Goal

A dish with a `harness:` block runs `petri seed` and `petri grow` end-to-end on pi. Done when #27's integration test passes on a pi-backed dish.

## Context

The pi wiring exists in the M1 backlog but is split across several issues, none named for the outcome. This tracking issue makes the chain explicit and self-contained: close every sub-issue below and pi works. The decision to move forward with pi was made after the validation spike (#17); see the evidence section below.

## The wiring chain (sub-issues, in order)

- [ ] #18 — error taxonomy and retry core: the typed failure vocabulary the transport maps into (also consumed by the claude-code adapter, #23)
- [ ] #20 — fake_pi stub and testing tiers: the offline stand-in every transport test runs against
- [ ] #21 — pi RPC transport: spawn `pi --mode rpc`, LF-JSONL framing, long-lived session, error mapping
- [ ] #22 — PiModel: pydantic-ai `Model` over the transport — request mapping, tool policy, structured output, usage capture
- [ ] #25 — harness resolution: `harness:` block → PiModel, `check_pi()` preflight, `petri init` default flip
- [ ] #26 — bridge part 1: the four decomposition-path methods on pydantic-ai Agents
- [ ] #27 — bridge part 2: assess_cell verdict discipline, match_evidence, and the CLI wiring — the end-to-end wire-up

#18 and #20 are the unblocked starting points; #21 is dependency-linked behind them. #18 is shared infrastructure — the claude-code adapter port (#23, outside this tracker) consumes it too.

## Evidence

The validated protocol contract and all spike data live on **closed PR #119** (https://github.com/onthemarkdata/petri/pull/119) — closed by decision and kept as the record; it stands in for the `docs/spikes/` paths cited in the sub-issues' bodies (`pi-rpc.md`, `pi_rpc_probe.py`, `transcripts/`, `pi-e2e-report.md`, `pi-e2e-evidence.md`, `harness-options.md`).

Key resolved answers: the RPC session executes commands serially, so the transport holds one in-flight request. Failures surface on three channels, including one that reports command-level success while the generation failed (`message.stopReason:"error"`). Usage and dollar cost arrive on every assistant message. Node ≥22.19 applies to the npm install path only; the standalone binary is the documented install.
